articles.headline: Why Diversification Still Matters
articles.summary: Diversification means spreading your money so one bad surprise does not hit everything at once.
articles.plainEnglish: Instead of putting all your money in one pocket, you use several pockets. If one pocket tears, you do not lose everything.
articles.whyItMatters: It lowers the chance that one stock, one sector, or one market shock can badly hurt your overall plan.
articles.everydayExample: It is like carrying water in a few smaller bottles instead of one giant bottle. If one slips, you still have the rest.
takeaways: Mixing assets helps smooth the ride.
Diversification does not remove risk, but it can reduce single-name risk.
It works best when the holdings are genuinely different from each other.

jargonBuster.meaning: Spreading money across different investments.

articles.headline: What Dividend Investors Should Watch
articles.summary: Good dividend investing is not just about chasing the biggest yield on the screen.
articles.plainEnglish: A very high dividend can be a gift or a warning sign. You want income that looks strong enough to keep being paid.
articles.whyItMatters: Investors often buy high yield names for safety, but unstable payouts can lead to capital losses and income disappointment.
articles.everydayExample: A shop offering a huge discount every day may be generous, or it may be struggling and trying to survive.
takeaways: Look at payout strength, not just headline yield.
Cashflow and balance sheet quality matter.
Slow, dependable growers can beat flashy income traps.
